headline.purpose: Section headings, panel titles, dialog headers.

body.purpose: Reading text, descriptions, PR body previews.

label.purpose: Section labels, data table column headers. Uppercase only at this size.

mono.purpose: All machine-readable values: hashes, IDs, paths, durations, log lines.

shadows.name: card-ambient
shadows.purpose: Default card boundary. Extremely subtle, establishes surface without lifting it.

shadows.name: floating
shadows.purpose: Command palette and full overlays. High opacity deliberate on dark theme.

shadows.name: glow-green
shadows.purpose: Accent glow for live-state emphasis. Rare.

shadows.name: glow-red
shadows.purpose: Incident-state glow. Use only on critical failure callouts.

motion.name: ease-standard
motion.purpose: Default easing for state transitions (sidebar width, card hover).

motion.name: ease-expo-out
motion.purpose: Drawer/overlay slide-in. Exponential deceleration for overlay entrances.

breakpoints.name: md
breakpoints.purpose: Tablet portrait. Sidebar switches from overlay drawer to static collapsed.

breakpoints.name: lg
breakpoints.purpose: Desktop. Content width widens to 82% then 75%.

breakpoints.name: 2xl
breakpoints.purpose: Large monitor. 75% content cap prevents over-stretching.

narrative.overview:
GitPulse's visual language is built on one principle: every pixel is paid rent by the information it carries. The system draws from physical instrument panels, not from web software convention. Controls are where you expect them. Readouts are legible at a glance. Color is a signal, not a decoration.

The density is intentional. DevOps engineers read data tables for a living; they triage failures at 2am under pressure; they need to scan and dismiss, not be guided through flows. The UI trusts the user to be competent and returns that trust with information, not reassurance.

The sharp-edged aesthetic enforces authority. All UI surfaces use 2-3px corner radii, reflecting a deliberate technical-document aesthetic: the precision of a hardware specification sheet, not a consumer app.
keyCharacteristics: Near-zero border-radius on all interactive surfaces (2-3px globally overridden)
Tonal surface layering as the primary depth mechanism; decorative shadows are prohibited
Pipeline Green is the sole accent; it appears only on live states, confirmations, and primary actions
Monospace type for all data values, IDs, hashes, paths, and machine-readable content
Status always carries dual indicators (dot plus label) independent of color

rules.name: The One Voice Rule
rules.body: Pipeline Green appears on at most 10% of any given screen. It marks live activity, confirmations, and primary actions. Using it decoratively destroys its signal value.

rules.name: The Red Finds You Rule
rules.body: Incident Red is never used for branding, decoration, or information. It appears only when a failure state demands attention.

rules.name: The Mono Rule
rules.body: Any value that could appear in a terminal uses monospace. Mixing proportional and monospace type within a data column creates misalignment.

rules.name: The Ring Rule
rules.body: Cards use ring-1 ring-border (1px structural outline) as the primary boundary. Border, outline, and box-shadow produce inconsistent results across layout contexts.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: Surfaces are flat at rest. The card ambient shadow is 1-pixel grade; it establishes the surface plane without lifting it. Elevation is earned through interaction state, not assumed.

dos: Do use Pipeline Green only for live states, confirmed outcomes, and primary actions.
Do display all data values, hashes, timestamps, durations, IDs, and paths in JetBrains Mono.
Do use ring-1 ring-border as the canonical card boundary.
Do ensure every status color has a secondary indicator (dot, label, or icon) for color-blind users.
Do keep corner radii at 2-3px on all interactive surfaces.
Do compress information intelligently. Whitespace separates groups; it does not pad individual elements.
donts: Don't replicate DataDog or Grafana's blue-grey enterprise grid aesthetic.
Don't use neon-on-black or RGB multi-accent schemes. Pipeline Green is the single accent.
Don't strip the UI to emptiness in the name of minimalism. Information density is a feature.
Don't use Notion or Linear visual language (pastel surfaces, soft rounding, consumer-app whitespace).
Don't use border-left or border-right greater than 1px as a colored accent stripe.
Don't use gradient text (background-clip: text with gradient background).
Don't add decorative charts or filler metric widgets.
Don't use modal dialogs as the first solution for any interaction.
Don't use success toasts or confirmation dialogs for routine actions.
